risks: Pre-mortem Q1 (two weeks later, slice failed review/validation — most likely cause): the extraction-triple-emission portion was built against src/distill/prompts/extract.ts before the still-in-draft D3 merged-extraction-prompt FEAT actually landed, producing either a hard merge conflict on the same file or a semantic mismatch (triples authored against the OLD atomic few-shot shape get invalidated the moment D3's richer-prompt rewrite lands), forcing a rework of the just-built slice.

Pre-mortem Q2 (this merged and broke the loop — what does rollback require?): mixed answer by component. The entity_relations table + migration is a plain new-table revert (git revert / drop table, no existing data reshaped, no cleanup needed) — safe. But if the extraction-triple emission is interleaved into the SAME commit/PR as the D3 prompt rewrite (which the design doc's own sequencing explicitly invites — '...lands inside 3.2's builder scope'), rollback requires manually disentangling two features' hunks out of one shared file rather than a clean revert — the coordination hazard becoming a real rollback cost, not just a review-time annoyance.

Pre-mortem Q3 (which existing test would NOT catch a regression here?): scripts/eval/recall-quality/run.mjs measures memory-retrieval MRR, not relation-triple correctness or entity_graph neighbor/timeline shape — there is no existing coverage anywhere in the repo for relation_type formatting (e.g. silently emitting free-text instead of the specified SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE) or for confidence-field semantics; either could regress silently through both the recall harness and the existing entity test suite.

Coordination/ownership risk (named directly by today's own design doc, quoted above): FEAT-481's core value-delivering piece (extraction wiring) is designed to be absorbed into a FEAT that does not yet exist as an approved backlog item (D3) — scoring FEAT-481 as a standalone, independently-sliceable epic right now risks PM inventing slice boundaries that get thrown away the moment D3 is actually filed.

Kill-list boundary risk: docs/research/2026-07-08-supermemory-matrix.md:19 records a prior deliberate decision that full graph-memory territory is out of scope ('entity layer only (kill-list: full graph)'). FEAT-481's entity_relations table + entity_graph MCP tool (neighbors + timeline) is structurally graph infrastructure even though it explicitly excludes graph algebra/path queries/community detection — an architect-level judgment call on which side of that line this FEAT falls is still open (design doc status: draft, pending architect + architect-reviewer), and PM scoring cannot substitute for that call.
